t: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.

fable.w: This is a standard appropriations limitation on how long funds stay available for obligation. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. There is no tempting contrary reading; nothing in the text concerns participation.
fable.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.

opus.w: This is standard appropriations wording: funds can only be committed during the current fiscal year unless the Act says otherwise. No one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting wrong reading:** None. This is standard appropriations wording about how long funds remain available. It mentions no outside party, consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
2. **Label:** No.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard fiscal provision limiting the availability of appropriated funds to the current fiscal year. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. It is an internal administrative rule regarding budget execution, not a mechanism for public or external participation.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "appropriations," it implicitly involves the public or contractors who receive funds, thus implying participation. However, this is a standard boilerplate provision regarding the expiration of funds (anti-deficiency rule) and does not establish any process for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. It is purely an internal fiscal constraint.
